correctness.rationale: The Riesz kernel test establishes H>0; direct Gaussian integration gives PP*=κ²C_D with a B-Hermitian positive D, diagonalized by a weighted change of variables. Boundedness, compactness, all exact singular products and Schatten sums follow. The d=2 irrational second-order law follows by uniform equidistribution of the irrational rotation of fractional parts; rational resonances are counted via a lattice triangle with exactly N+1 boundary solutions. A standalone rational checker confirms noncommuting 2×2 determinant/trace identities and finite rational counts. The proof handles strict count conventions and every quantifier.

value.rationale: Exact approximation and Schatten spectra quantify the rate of finite-rank approximation of the natural off-diagonal Fock projection; noncommuting Gaussian anisotropy is intrinsic rather than an arbitrary slice. The arithmetic transition is a sharp nontrivial boundary: its second-order eigenvalue count exists for irrational log-ratio but provably cannot exist for rational log-ratio, with explicit finite threshold multiplicities. The same natural family also reveals the precise operator-norm/compactness thresholds. It is not an invented parameter perturbation or an unsupported 1D numerical gain.
